# How it works

gx adds a context layer around your existing Git workflow. It captures what
happened during coding sessions, attaches that context to ordinary Git commits,
and uses it for two review surfaces: `gx review` locally and generated PR
summaries on GitHub.

## The problem

Git was built for humans typing commits one at a time. A commit stores a
snapshot and a short message, and for human-paced work that is usually enough.

Agent-written code breaks two of Git's assumptions:

1. **The context that explains a change never makes it into the repo.** The
   prompt that asked for the change, the commands the agent ran, the tests it
   executed, the dead ends it backed out of — all of that lives in a session
   transcript that is gone by review time. The commit message is whatever one
   line survived.
2. **Review is now the bottleneck.** The cost of generating code is dropping
   toward zero, but teams still review line by line. When a pull request is one
   large undifferentiated diff with a thin message, the reviewer reconstructs
   intent from scratch.

## What gx captures

- **Sessions** — transcripts from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. The pre-push
  hook captures them into `~/.gx/gx.db` and publishes them alongside
  the code they produced.
- **Revisions** — each plain `git commit` is recorded as one reviewable unit,
  down to individual hunks. gx links each revision to the session that
  produced it by matching the changed hunks against captured session activity —
  nothing is attached by hand.

## How gx review works

`gx review` reads the current change — a dirty working tree, or the branch's
commits against its base — and reviews it with two independent AI reviewers
plus repo context: the indexed codebase, captured sessions, review history, and
your repo's review policy. A judge model then verifies and dedupes the
findings.

Each surviving finding is printed with **Why** (the defect), **Do next** (the
concrete fix), and its sources. When both reviewers raised the same issue
independently, the report says so — that agreement is the strongest confidence
signal a two-model panel produces.

The command writes nothing — no hooks, no repo state, no index mutation — so it
runs anywhere, including CI (`--fail-on` turns it into a gate) and checkouts
you do not own. See the [CLI reference](/docs/cli#gx-review).

## How PR summaries work

On `git push`, the pre-push hook uploads a review bundle: the revisions, their
hunks, and the linked sessions. When a pull request exists, gx Cloud
generates a summary from that bundle plus the indexed codebase, and writes it
into the PR description below your own text.

The summary opens with a verdict — 🟢 **Quick scan**, 🟡 **Careful pass**, or
🔴 **Deep review** — judged by blast radius: what the change can break,
including code the diff never touches. Notable Changes each carry an
`Attribution:` line naming the concrete source that informed them. See
[Pull Requests](/docs/pull-requests).

## Why this speeds up review

- The verdict tells a reviewer how much attention a PR needs before they open
  the diff. A two-file rename that breaks downstream consumers gets 🔴; a
  contained refactor gets 🟢.
- Notable Changes point at the hunks that decide correctness, so the mechanical
  rest can be skimmed instead of read line by line.
- Session provenance answers "why is this here?" without a round-trip to the
  author — the prompt, commands, and tests are part of the review context.
- `gx review` catches findings before the PR exists, when they are cheapest to
  fix.

## Everything is still just Git

The hooks publish normal Git branches and commits; sessions and metadata go to
gx Cloud as a review bundle. Nothing about your repository becomes
gx-specific — if you stop using gx tomorrow, your branches and
commits remain ordinary Git.

---

# Getting Started

gx records which agent session produced each Git commit and uses that context
for AI code review and generated pull request summaries. You work in plain Git.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
```

This installs bash/zsh completions and aliases, like `gxr`, for `gx review`.

## Basic Usage

You run exactly two gx commands: `gx init` once per repository to install the
Git hooks, and `gx review` whenever you want an AI review. Otherwise, use Git
as normal — the hooks record revisions, capture sessions, and publish on push
without any gx-specific commands.

```bash
cd your-repo
gx init                                # once per repo: installs the Git hooks
git add src/retry.js
git commit -m "add retry helper"       # hook records the revision
gx review                              # AI review before you push (optional)
git push                               # hook captures the session and publishes
gh pr create                           # gx Cloud adds the summary to the PR
```

## Uninstall

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/gx ~/.local/bin/gxr ~/.local/bin/gx-mcp
rm -f ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/gx ~/.zfunc/_gx
```

Installed Git hooks exit silently when the binary is absent, so plain Git keeps
working. Local data remains in `~/.gx`.

## Pages

- [CLI](/docs/cli) — every command: `gx init`, `gx review`, `gx auth`, `gx doctor`
- [MCP](/docs/mcp) — connect `gx_review` to Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- [Pull Requests](/docs/pull-requests) — generated PR summaries and `@gx` chat on GitHub

---

# CLI

Initialize any repository with `gx init`. This installs git hooks that capture
your session context and pairs it with your code changes, giving gx
better context for review.

## gx CLI Overview

```bash
gx init         # set up hooks in a repo (run once)
gx review       # AI review of the current change (alias: gxr)
gx constraints  # pre-ship exit gate for the current change (alias: gxc)
gx auth         # sign in to gx Cloud
gx doctor       # diagnose capture, hooks, and publishing
gx version      # print the version
```

## gx init

```bash
gx init
```

`gx init` installs the Git hooks and registers the MCP server. Run it once per
repository.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | user name to store in gx config (defaults to Git identity) |
| `--email <email>` | user email to store in gx config |
| `-y`, `--yes` | accept defaults and suppress prompts — use in scripts and agent sandboxes |
| `--global` | install the hooks machine-wide instead of for one repository |

### Global hooks

```bash
gx init --global
```

Installs the hooks once for every repository. The scripts chain to each
repository's own hooks of the same name, so husky, lefthook, and hand-written
hooks keep working. If a global hooks path is already set to something else,
`gx init --global` stops rather than overwriting it.

Opt a single repository out, from inside it:

```bash
git config gx.enabled false
```

Undo the machine-wide install:

```bash
git config --global --unset core.hooksPath
```

## gx review

```bash
gx review                                 # alias: gxr
gx review "check the auth rollback path"
gx review --scope security                # focused pass
gx review --focus src/auth --deep         # deep review of one directory
```

Reviews the current codebase state. `gx review` uses your indexed codebases,
two separate models to identify the most important issues with a judge to
dedupe findings. This can be run in the terminal or via [MCP](/docs/mcp).

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[prompt]` | optional positional prompt to steer the review |
| `--base <ref>` | review the commit range `<ref>...HEAD` instead of the working tree |
| `--scope <name>` | focused lens: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `--focus <path>` | limit the review to files under a path prefix |
| `--repo` | review the whole repository rather than the current change |
| `--deep` | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `--verbose` | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |
| `--json` | print the report as JSON |
| `--fail-on <level>` | exit non-zero when findings at or above this level survive |
| `--no-publish` | skip posting the PR review comment and recording review history |

### What gets reviewed

1. `--base <ref>` when given — the range `<ref>...HEAD`
2. Otherwise a dirty working tree
3. Otherwise the branch's commits against an auto-detected base (`main`,
   `master`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`), or the last commit when HEAD is
   the base branch

If nothing was found, `gx review` says so. "Nothing was reviewed" is its own
outcome and never counts as a clean pass.

### Read-only

`gx review` does not mutate any logic, and doesn't require `gx init`
(`gx init` is required for PR summaries and chat).

### As a CI gate

```bash
gx review --base origin/main --fail-on strong --no-publish
```

`--fail-on` fails the review when findings at or above the level survive:

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | never fail (default) |
| `any` | fail on anything the review raised |
| `speculative` | findings at `speculative` strength or above |
| `worth-exploring` | findings at `worth-exploring` strength or above |
| `strong` | findings at `strong` strength or above |
| `blocking` | only findings that should stop a merge |

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | reviewed, and nothing at or above the threshold survived |
| `3` | findings at or above the threshold survived |
| `4` | nothing was reviewed — a gate should not pass without inspecting code |

Pair with `--no-publish` so CI never posts PR comments, and `--json` to parse
findings yourself.

## gx constraints

```bash
gx constraints                       # alias: gxc
gx constraints "fix auth timeout"    # state the intent for the back-pressure gate
gx constraints --verbose             # list the source files behind each gate
gx constraints --md                  # markdown report (what agents relay)
```

The pre-ship exit gate. Checks the current change against six constraints and
reports PASS, FAIL, or SKIPPED for each, plus a ship / no-ship verdict — run
it before opening a PR. Deterministic checks decide what they can; one AI
judgment call covers the rest, grounded in the same indexed context
`gx review` uses.

| Gate | What it checks |
| --- | --- |
| Correctness | the project's own tests and builds: `go test`, `tsc`, `cargo check`, `dotnet build`, `flutter analyze`, `pytest` |
| Security | secrets in added lines; dependency audits (`govulncheck`, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`, `cargo audit`) |
| Code health | linters, reviewability (large changes warn, they don't block), and whether tests accompany the sources |
| Back-pressure | is every part of the change in service of the stated intent — scope creep, regenerated bloat, unjustified new dependencies |
| Accessibility | added UI elements stay usable by keyboard and screen reader; auto-skips when no UI files changed |
| Performance | hot-path regressions on perf-relevant changes; the model must justify a pass explicitly |

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[intent]` | optional positional statement of what the change is meant to do |
| `--base <ref>` | check the commit range `<ref>...HEAD` instead of the working tree |
| `--verbose` | list the source files behind each gate |
| `--md` | print the report as markdown |
| `--json` | print the full report as JSON |
| `--skip-gates <list>` | comma-separated gates to skip |
| `--timeout <dur>` | whole-run budget (default 5m) |
| `--report-only` | always exit 0; read the verdict from the report |

Findings show the source lines being discussed, syntax-highlighted, and every
report ends with a How to resolve section: one numbered step per finding with
the code and the fix. A missing tool is never a failure — an auditor that
isn't installed or can't reach its database is reported as skipped evidence.

The exit code is the gate by default — no opt-in flag needed:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | ship — every gate passed or was legitimately skipped |
| `3` | no-ship — at least one gate failed |
| `4` | nothing to check — a gate should not pass without inspecting code |
| `5` | degraded — the AI gates could not run, so a pass would be unearned |

Use `--report-only` to opt out of the coded exits and read the verdict from
the report instead.

## gx auth

```bash
gx auth login
gx auth status
gx auth logout
```

Signs the CLI into gx Cloud through GitHub.

## gx doctor

```bash
gx doctor            # diagnose capture, hooks, auth, and the publish queue
gx doctor --fix      # apply safe repairs
gx doctor --json     # machine-readable report
gx doctor --report   # send this diagnosis and recent logs to support
```

## gx version

```bash
gx version
gx version --json
```

## Shortcuts

The installer links `gxr` and `gxc` to the same binary:

```bash
gxr   # gx review
gxc   # gx constraints
```

---

# MCP

The MCP server ships with the CLI as a local stdio binary. It shells out to the
CLI, so repo state stays on your machine. It exposes two tools: `gx_review`
and `gx_constraints`.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
```

## Register with your agent

`gx init` registers the server automatically with agent CLIs found on your
`PATH` (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and reports something like
`MCP ok: Claude Code, Cursor`.

To register with every MCP client on your machine in one command, use
[`add-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/add-mcp):

```bash
npx add-mcp @satoricorp/gx --name gx -g -y
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-g` | install user-level so gx is available in every project; omit for project-level config |
| `-y` | non-interactive (skip prompts) |
| `-a <agent>` | target a specific agent (repeatable), e.g. `-a cursor` |

Most clients load MCP servers at startup — restart the client or open a new
chat after registering.

For clients neither path covers, the stdio shape is:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gx": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@satoricorp/gx"]
    }
  }
}
```

The server finds the CLI in `~/.local/bin` or on `PATH`; set `GX_BINARY`
to point somewhere else.

## gx_review

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | optional reviewer prompt, e.g. `"check auth rollback risks"` |
| `scope` | enum | focused lens: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `focus` | string | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `deep` | boolean | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `verbose` | boolean | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |
| `repo` | boolean | review the whole repository instead of the current change |
| `cwd` | string | repository working directory (defaults to the MCP server process cwd) |

Runs `gx review` with `--no-publish` always set, so an agent asking for review
context never comments on a pull request. It is read-only and never initializes
a repository. May run up to 5 minutes.

Saving and publishing are plain Git, not MCP calls: `git add` + `git commit`
record the revision through the hooks, `git push` captures and publishes.

## gx_constraints

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | optional intent hint, e.g. `"fix auth timeout"` — the back-pressure gate judges scope against it |
| `verbose` | boolean | list the source files behind each gate |
| `cwd` | string | repository working directory (defaults to the MCP server process cwd) |

The pre-ship exit gate: checks the current change against six constraints —
correctness, security, code health, back-pressure, accessibility,
performance — and returns a markdown report with a ship / no-ship verdict.
Agents run it before opening a PR and relay the report.

Always runs `gx constraints --report-only --md`, so a no-ship verdict is a
successful tool call, not an error — the verdict lives in the report's final
`Verdict:` / `Next:` lines, with a How to resolve section of per-finding
fixes above them. Read-only and never initializes a repository. May run up to
6 minutes when the project's test suite is slow.

## AGENTS.md instructions

`gx init` offers to append these instructions to your repo's `AGENTS.md`. If you
skipped that step, add them manually:

```markdown
Version control: plain Git. Once `gx init` installs the hooks, gx records
and publishes automatically — there is no gx save verb.

Default flow:
- Run `git add` to stage the files for this revision.
- Run `git commit -m "..."` to save. An gx hook records the commit as a reviewable revision.
- Run plain `git push` to publish. The gx pre-push hook captures the session and
  publishes automatically — do not run `gx push` or `gx capture push` yourself.
- Open PRs with `gh pr create` (or the GitHub UI). Do not seed a `## Summary` in the
  PR body — leave human notes only; gx Cloud appends the rich summary below.
- To amend, use `git commit --amend` and preserve the gx revision trailer in the message.

For AI review, run the `gx_review` MCP tool (or the `gx review` CLI) on the current change.
Before shipping, run the `gx_constraints` MCP tool (or `gx constraints`) to check the change
against the pre-ship constraint gates.
```

---

# Pull Requests

gx Cloud writes a review summary into your pull request description and
answers questions when you mention `@gx` in PR comments.

A summary looks like this:

```markdown
> 🔴 👀 **Deep review** — clean rename in this repo, but indexed consumers still read the old field

Renames `amount_cents` → `amount` in the `payment.settled` event payload and
updates the emitter and its tests. Internally consistent — the risk is entirely
downstream.

## Blast Radius

🔴 HIGH (2 files, 1 area, +18/-11 lines).
3 consumers in `billing-dashboard` and `revenue-export` still read
`amount_cents` and default to 0 on a missing field.

## Notable Changes

- Renamed `amount_cents` → `amount` in the settled-event payload
  Attribution: codebase `internal/events/settled.go:34`
- Old field still read by 3 cross-repo consumers; none updated in this PR
  Attribution: codebase `billing-dashboard/src/ingest/settlement.ts:88`

*Generated by gx.*
```

## Setup

1. `gx auth login` (or sign in on the console)
2. Install the gx GitHub App on your account or organization:
   [github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx](https://github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx)
3. Publish through the hook: `git push` in a repo where `gx init` ran

A PR whose branch was never pushed through the pre-push hook gets no summary —
there is no captured context to summarize.

## PR summaries

The summary is written into the **pull request description**, not a comment.
Your own text stays above the gx block; regeneration replaces only the
block. Do not seed a `## Summary` section — leave the body for your own notes.

What each section is:

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict line | 🟢 **Quick scan** (LOW) / 🟡 **Careful pass** (MEDIUM) / 🔴 **Deep review** (HIGH), plus a one-line triage reason. The label always matches the Blast Radius level |
| Overview | one paragraph: what changed and why |
| Blast Radius | severity with file/area/line counts and a risk note. Judged by what the change can break — including code the diff never touches — not by diff size |
| Notable Changes | the changes a reviewer should look at first, each with an `Attribution:` line naming the concrete source: a codebase path, a captured agent session, a prior PR, or docs |

Summaries are generated when the GitHub App sees `pull_request`
`opened`/`synchronize` for a branch with published gx context, and after a
publish when a PR already exists. Push again to force a refresh.

## Chat with @gx

Mention `@gx` in any PR comment:

```text
@gx which files should I review first?
@gx explain the auth callback changes
@gx what is the highest-risk change in this PR?
@gx are there missing tests?
```

Answers cite their sources: published revision diffs, changed hunks, PR comments,
the latest summary, and — when available — captured session context, indexed
codebase context, and previous findings. Because revisions carry session
provenance, `@gx` can answer what the author asked for and which commands and
tests ran.

### Retire a learned rule

```text
@gx skip rule never use var
@gx do not enforce this migration naming rule
```

When a matching active rule exists, it is retired and the override recorded.
Requires **write**, **maintain**, or **admin** permission on the repository.

---

# gx changelog: new features, updates, and fixes

## July 29, 2026

**PR summary verdict labels** — The summary's triage line now states what the reader
must do, not just a color: 🟢 **Quick scan** (LOW), 🟡 **Careful pass** (MEDIUM),
🔴 **Deep review** (HIGH). The label is enforced server-side to always match the
Blast Radius level, so a red summary can never read as permission to skim.

**gx** — The product formerly known as gx is now gx. The CLI is `gx`
(`gxr` for one-shot review, `gx-mcp` for agents). Install from
`download.gx.run`; docs live at `docs.gx.run`.

## July 26, 2026

**Plain Git is the whole workflow** — Capture and publishing are entirely hook-driven:
`git commit` records a revision, `git push` captures the session and publishes. The
porcelain that duplicated Git (`gx push`, `gx sync`, the background daemon, and the
macOS menu-bar app) has been removed. If you have an older install, `gx init` cleans
up the retired pieces.

**PR summaries write to the description** — gx Cloud writes the rich summary
into the pull request description below your own text, behind an gx-owned
marker. Your notes survive every regeneration.

**`gx review` is guaranteed read-only** — Review writes nothing: no repo state, no
`.git/index` mutation, no `~/.gx` on machines that never ran `gx`, and no
uploads when a gate fails. `--fail-on` turns a review into a CI gate with distinct
exit codes for "findings survived" and "nothing was reviewed". See the
[CLI reference](/docs/cli#gx-review).

**Two-model review panel** — `gx review` runs two independent Anthropic reviewers
plus a judge that verifies and dedupes findings. When both reviewers flag the same
issue independently, the report says so — the strongest confidence signal a panel
produces.

## July 2, 2026

**Generated GitHub PR summaries** — After you publish with plain `git push` and open
a PR, gx Cloud posts a generated review summary highlighting blast radius and
high-impact review targets.

**Code review history memory** — `gx review` pulls in indexed context from your past
reviews and GitHub comment history, and attaches review policy context so findings
stay consistent with how your team reviews code.

**Prompted `gx review`** — Trigger `gx review` with a targeted prompt to focus the
review on a specific concern instead of the full default sweep.
